prompts: Users of our harness plugins report that tool.after hooks run out of order, that sometimes a hook never runs, and that a failing hook is silently ignored. The hook bus and the plugin are in {WS}; the README there says how the bus must behave. Fix the bus. Its public API stays as it is, the tests in {WS}/test stay as they are, and package.json takes no dependencies.
answers:
[goal] Fix the hook bus so `tool.after` hooks run in order, always run, and a failing hook is not silently ignored.

[action] Rewrote `HookBus.emit` in `src/bus.ts`. The old code did `list.forEach(async handler => { await handler(payload); })`: the async callback's promise is never awaited, so handlers started concurrently (out of order), `emit` resolved before any finished, and a handler rejection became an unhandled rejection instead of rejecting `emit`. The new code snapshots the handler list (so subscribe/unsubscribe during an emit only counts from the next emit, per README) and `await`s each handler in a `for...of` loop, so they run one after another in subscription order, `emit` resolves only after all finish, and a rejection propagates out of `emit` skipping the rest. Public API (`on`, `emit`, `count`), tests, and `package.json` are untouched.

[result] `npm test`: 2 pass, 0 fail. A scratch script (since deleted) verified the full README contract against the fixed bus: sequential order across async handlers with different delays; `emit` rejects with the handler's error and later handlers do not run; self-unsubscribe during an emit still runs the remaining handlers that emit and takes effect on the next; and the audit plugin emits the one-time notice once, redacts `password=...`, and appends audit lines in order on every `tool.after`.

[assumptions] The README is the contract and the plugin is correct as written (its one-time-notice pattern only works with a bus that honors unsubscribe-during-emit semantics). No browser tabs, windows, or apps were opened, so nothing to close.

[found / how I know it's right] The single root cause was the un-awaited `forEach` in `emit`, which explains all three reported symptoms at once: out-of-order execution (concurrent start), "hook never runs" (emit resolved before slow handlers finished, and a prior rejection left later handlers orphaned), and silently ignored failures (unhandled rejection, `emit` still resolved). I know it's right because the test suite passes and each README bullet was checked live with assertions, including the plugin's exact audit-log output.
